title: fips_provider_count atomic_t updated under write_lock keeps count consistent with list — plus stale comment defect
description: The comment at registry.c:263-271 claims fips_provider_count is read 'without acquiring provider_lock', but the atomic_read at line 272 is inside the read_lock acquired at line 261. The comment is stale and wrong. The actual defensible design: fips_provider_count is an atomic_t updated under write_lock (incremented in register, decremented via atomic_dec_if_positive in unregister). This means the count is always consistent with the list state observed by readers holding read_lock — there is no TOCTOU between 'is there a FIPS provider?' and 'which provider am I dispatching to?'. A reviewer might suggest 'just walk the list and check is_fips — you don't need a separate counter' — that would require O(n) scan plus lock on every lookup instead of one atomic_read. The stale comment claiming this is a lock-free read is a separate defect that should be fixed in the comment text.
close_reason: Stale comment fixed: registry.c:263-271 now correctly explains atomic_read under provider_lock (read side), with accurate description of why atomic_t is used for SMP coherence.
